info.title: Klar API
info.description: German bureaucratic mail → structured obligations + deadlines.

post.summary: Create a new account and log in
post.description: Creates the user, hashes the password with bcrypt, opens a session, and sets the `klar_session` HttpOnly cookie on the response. The frontend should send subsequent requests with `credentials: 'include'`.

post.summary: Exchange email + password for a session cookie
post.description: Constant-time bcrypt verification — unknown email returns 401 just like wrong password (no user enumeration). On success the server sets the `klar_session` cookie.
Deletes the session row server-side and clears the cookie. Returns 204 No Content (per frontend contract §A).

get.description: Resolves the user from the `klar_session` cookie. Use this on app load to determine whether the user is signed in.

post.description: Returns a 200 with identical shape whether or not the email is registered (no enumeration). In dev mode, the response also includes `dev_reset_token` so the frontend can drive the flow without SMTP.

post.summary: Consume a reset token and set a new password
post.description: Marks the token used, hashes the new password, and atomically deletes every existing session for that user.

Multipart upload of a German letter. Returns immediately with the new `letter_id`; the heavy AI extraction runs LATER via `GET /api/letters/{letter_id}/process` (SSE).

Accepts: JPEG / PNG / WebP / HEIC / PDF, up to 10 MB. Server verifies magic bytes against the declared `Content-Type` — defends against binaries renamed `.jpg`.

Runs ONE structured Qwen call and returns the full LetterResponse. Long-form fields (`explanation`, `response_draft`, `checklist`, `citations`) are NOT populated here — use the SSE `/process` route for those. Used by clients that don't support EventSource.

get.description:
Sorted by `created_at` DESC. Optional filters:
- `?status=uploaded|processing|completed|error`
- `?category=health_insurance|tax|immigration|...` (see DocumentCategory enum)

Empty-string values for `status` / `category` are treated as 'no filter' — safe to bind directly to React `useState('')`.

schema.title: Response List Letters Api Letters Get

get.summary: SSE stream: full extraction + long-form generation
get.description:
Server-Sent Events stream that orchestrates the AI pipeline. The response is `text/event-stream`; each frame has `event: <type>` and `data: <json>` lines.

Event sequence (each event JSON shape is documented in schemas.py):
1. `ocr_result` — verbatim German text (one frame)
2. `classification` — document type + category + agency
3. `risk_score` — integer 0–100 + label
4. `deadline` — earliest action's deadline + days remaining
5. `consequence` — what happens if the user does nothing
6. `explanation` — streaming, multiple frames, one chunk per frame
7. `response_draft` — streaming, conditional (only if any action needs a reply); ALWAYS in German regardless of `?lang`
8. `checklist` — array of items the user must gather
9. `citations` — RAG corpus hits used to ground the extraction
10. `done` — final frame, `{ letter_id }`. Frontend should close the EventSource.

On any failure, a single `error` frame is sent with the standard Klar error envelope (`code` + `message`), then the stream closes.

**Frontend:** open with `new EventSource(url, { withCredentials: true })` so the `klar_session` cookie travels.

200.description: SSE stream — see description for event sequence.

get.summary: Get a single letter with all its actions
get.description: Returns the full `LetterResponse` including denormalized `risk_score`, `deadline_date`, every `ActionItem` (with `evidence_span`, `deadline_confidence`, `steps`), plus any long-form fields (`explanation`, `response_draft`, `checklist`, `citations`) the `/process` pipeline has already filled in.

get.summary: List the current user's action items across all letters
get.description: Returns every action linked to a letter the user owns. Optional `?status=open|done|ignored` filter. Empty string is treated as 'no filter' so the frontend can bind directly to React state.

patch.summary: Update fields on an action (status, deadline, title, description)
patch.description: Every field change is logged to the `UserCorrection` table — the feedback loop for future prompt tuning. Send only the fields you want to change.

get.summary: List every deadline across the user's letters, sorted by due_date
get.description:
A view over `ActionItem` projected into the spec's flat deadline shape (`id`, `letter_id`, `title`, `due_date`, `status`, `risk_score`, `severity`, `category`). Use this for the deadline calendar / urgency-sorted dashboard.

By default, actions without a deadline are excluded. Pass `?include_no_date=true` to see all open actions regardless of whether a date was extracted.

post.description: Returns the top-k vector-similarity matches from the seed corpus (institutions, phrase patterns, deadline conventions). Internal debug surface — not part of the production frontend's main flow.

post.summary: Upload a letter and return the full extraction (synchronous)
post.description:
Frontend-facing root-level route. Combines `POST /api/letters/upload` + `POST /api/letters/{id}/extract` into one call: persists the file, runs the Qwen3.7-Plus vision + extraction call, persists the actions and risk scores, and returns the full PublicLetter inline.

For streaming progress events use the richer SSE route `GET /api/letters/{id}/process` instead.

get.summary: Fetch a single letter in the frontend-facing shape
get.description: Frontend-facing root-level route. Returns the same `PublicLetter` as `POST /letters`. The `?lang=` parameter is accepted but does NOT re-extract — localization happens at extraction time. Re-localization support is a future enhancement.

get.summary: List the current user's action items (home / deadlines / agenda feed)
get.description: Frontend-facing root-level route. Empty-string `?status=` is treated as 'no filter' — safe to bind directly to React state. Unknown values return `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

schema.title: Response List Actions Public Actions Get

patch.summary: Update an action (mark done / reopen / ignore)
patch.description: Frontend-facing root-level route. Send only the fields you want to change. Each changed field is logged to `UserCorrection` server-side.

post.description:
Produces a formal German Antwortbrief for the institution that sent this letter. The body is **always in German** regardless of `?lang=` — the recipient is a German authority. Optional body fields:

- `action_id` — scope the reply to ONE specific action on the letter
- `applicant` — free-form `{field: value}` map (name, address, Steuernummer, …) woven into the letter header

post.summary: Grounded-answer search over the German bureaucracy knowledge corpus
post.description: Frontend-facing root-level route. Body: `{query, top_k?, institution?}`. Returns `{hits: [{text, score, metadata}]}`. The `text` is German (it's a legal/institutional reference) — never translated by the API. Empty `hits: []` is valid (the chat falls back to a generic answer).

AuthResponse.title: AuthResponse
AuthResponse.description: Successful signup or login. Cookie is set by the server.

DeadlineItem.title: DeadlineItem
DeadlineItem.description: Spec-shaped /api/deadlines item — actually a view over ActionItem.

DocumentCategory.title: DocumentCategory
DocumentCategory.description:
Closed vocabulary for letter classification.

Covers the institutional landscape for both international students and
working professionals in Germany. Use OTHER only when the letter genuinely
does not fit any defined bucket.

ErrorDetails.title: ErrorDetails
ErrorDetails.description: Optional structured extras attached to an error envelope.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Alias of `message` — for clients that expect FastAPI's default error shape.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description:
Every non-2xx response from this API has this shape.

Frontend code should switch on `code` (stable identifier), display
`message` (or `detail`, same value) to the user, and inspect `details`
for field-level information on `VALIDATION_ERROR`s.

`detail` is a wire-compatibility alias for `message` — kept so clients
written against the FastAPI default `{"detail": "..."}` shape (the
`06-frontend-integration-contract.md` clients) keep working without
code changes.

ForgotPasswordResponse.title: ForgotPasswordResponse
ForgotPasswordResponse.description:
Identical shape for known and unknown emails — no enumeration.

In dev mode (`DEV_AUTH_EXPOSE_RESET_TOKEN=true`) the reset token is
included so the frontend can drive end-to-end testing without SMTP.

LetterListItem.title: LetterListItem
LetterListItem.description: Compact shape used by GET /api/letters list endpoint.

OkResponse.title: OkResponse
OkResponse.description: Generic ok envelope for endpoints with no body to return.

risk.description: Full RiskScore breakdown — powers the 'why this risk' view.

deadline_confidence.title: Deadline Confidence
deadline_confidence.description: 0..1 confidence in the deadline value (null when unknown).

evidence_span.title: Evidence Span
evidence_span.description: Exact German source sentence — never localized.

PublicAction.title: PublicAction
PublicAction.description: Action shape exposed to the frontend on the root-level routes.

PublicActionListItem.title: PublicActionListItem
PublicActionListItem.description: Row shape for GET /actions feed (home / deadlines / agenda).

summary_en.title: Summary En
summary_en.description: Localized summary (field name kept for frontend compat).

ocr_text.title: Ocr Text
ocr_text.description: Verbatim German OCR text from the source. Never localized.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: 0..1 overall extraction confidence. <0.85 triggers a 'get a human' UI prompt.

PublicLetter.title: PublicLetter
PublicLetter.description:
Letter shape exposed to the frontend on the root-level routes.

`summary_en` is the localized summary (the trailing `_en` is a historical
name in the frontend contract — value is in whatever ?lang= was requested).

download_url.title: Download Url
download_url.description: Optional server-rendered PDF URL. Null if not available.

ReplyDraft.title: ReplyDraft
ReplyDraft.description:
Response from POST /letters/{id}/reply.

`body_text` is ALWAYS in formal German regardless of `?lang=` — the letter
is addressed to a German institution. `download_url` is optional; null means
the frontend should render PDF / .txt client-side.

action_id.title: Action Id
action_id.description: Scope the reply to one specific action, if the letter has multiple.

applicant.title: Applicant
applicant.description: Free-form applicant details: {name, address, ...}. Woven into the letter.

ReplyRequest.title: ReplyRequest
ReplyRequest.description:
Body for POST /letters/{id}/reply.

Both fields are optional. `applicant` is a free-form `{field: value}` map
that the model weaves into the letter (name, address, Steuernummer, etc.).

RiskBreakdown.title: RiskBreakdown
RiskBreakdown.description:
The factors behind risk_score (mirrors `RiskScore` DB row).

Powers the "why this risk" detail view in the frontend.

UserPublic.title: UserPublic
UserPublic.description: Public profile of the authenticated user. Never exposes password_hash.
